elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim" — express defence obligation running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Same sentence: indemnify and hold harmless "Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "an allegation that the Services or any Deliverable infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "Vendor's breach of Applicable Law", using the defined term in § 1.2.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (d): "Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party notice of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "the indemnifying Party shall control the defence".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: § 20.1 as rendered: "Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from third-party claims to the extent arising out of Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of Applicable Law" — the original open-ended "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services" is gone.

reasons: All ten preferred elements are met in operative language: the inserted paragraph creates an express Vendor defend/indemnify/hold-harmless duty to Customer and its Affiliates covering IP infringement of the Services or any Deliverable, Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data, and Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with a notice / control-of-defence / reasonable-cooperation procedure, and § 20.1 is narrowed to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law. The redline is position-complete at the preferred level.

The fallback level is not met and does not need to be: the rendered text contains no procure-continued-use / modify / replace remedy, no refund of applicable fees where those remedies are unavailable, and no 3x annual-fee super-cap on Vendor's indemnity. The three 'may exclude' items (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) are permissive allowances rather than obligations, so their absence is Customer-favourable, but the three affirmative fallback requirements are simply missing. If the drafter ever needs to fall back, the operative text must add: (i) 'Vendor shall, at its expense, procure the right to continue use, modify, or replace the infringing item, and if none is commercially reasonable, refund fees paid for the affected Services'; and (ii) an express '3x the fees paid in the twelve months preceding the claim' super-cap.

Minimality holds. The only changes are the narrowing edit required by the Customer-indemnity element and a concise insertion for a wholly missing Vendor indemnity; the drafter retained the existing 'defend, indemnify, and hold harmless' formulation, added no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no extra damages categories, and no procedure or boilerplate beyond the notice/control/cooperation mechanic the preferred checklist expressly requires. Omitting 'reasonable attorneys' fees' from the model language does not defeat any element.

Intent is preserved: § 9.3's termination trigger, the § 20 heading structure, and unrelated allocation and remedies survive without contradiction, and no favourable Customer language was deleted. Two drafting hygiene points to raise with the counterparty rather than defects in the elements: (a) § 9.3 still cross-refers to 'the remedies required by Section 20.5', which does not exist — this dangling reference pre-dates the redline, but the insertion is the natural place to cure it (numbering the new paragraph and adding the procure/modify/replace/refund ladder as 20.5 would fix both); and (b) the insertion uses capitalised 'Affiliates', 'Customer Data' and 'Deliverable' — confirm each is a defined term in the Definitions article, and if 'Affiliate' is not defined, use lower-case 'affiliates' to avoid introducing an undefined term.
